approval.trigger: No review gate is described anywhere in Linear's OAuth docs before end users can authorize an app. The optional Integration Directory listing is discretionary and discovery-only: submit a form plus icon/showcase assets, and Linear accepts integrations it thinks 'are useful to the community and are built by formal companies' (scripts, low-effort/vibe-coded, and hobbyist apps are generally not accepted). No stated timeline, cost, or user cap. For actor=app installs, the customer's workspace admin must complete installation.
approval.wait: None for connections; directory review duration not stated

blockers.detail: A client credentials token request with DIFFERENT scopes revokes and replaces all existing app-actor tokens for the app (the cap is 1000 active tokens in parallel, provided each uses the same scopes). One careless scope change can kill every running automation.
blockers.howToClear: Standardize your client-credentials scope set and never vary it per run.
blockers.title: Client-credentials scope changes nuke all app tokens

blockers.detail: 'Integrations using the actor=app mode are not able to also request admin scope.' If your agent design needs admin-level endpoints, the app-user identity cannot have them; you must act as a user instead.
blockers.howToClear: Decide the identity model (app user vs as-user) against your endpoint needs before building.
blockers.title: actor=app cannot take the admin scope

blockers.detail: 'The team access available to your app can be changed or revoked at any time by workspace admins' (an optional PermissionChange webhook exists). Access is a living grant, not a one-time setup.
blockers.howToClear: Subscribe to PermissionChange events and treat access loss as a normal state, not an error.
blockers.title: Workspace admins can shrink your access anytime

flavor.recommended: An OAuth2 Application created inside a Linear workspace (Settings > API), authorization code flow; choose the actor deliberately: actor=user to act as each connecting user, actor=app for a persistent agent identity
flavor.why: Linear's own guidance: 'If you're building an application for others to use, we recommend you use OAuth2 authentication.' With actor=app, the app exists in the customer workspace as an app user: it can be @mentioned, assigned/delegated issues, and reply to comments, and agents do not count as billable users. Linear highly recommends a dedicated workspace to own the app, since every admin of that workspace gets access to it.

name: Linear
nuances: Access tokens are valid 24 hours (expires_in 86399). All OAuth2 apps were migrated to the new refresh token system on April 1, 2026: refreshing returns a new access AND new refresh token, with a 30-minute grace window to replay the original request after network errors.
Client-credentials app tokens have access to all public teams in the workspace, and Linear's guidance is to request a fresh token at the start of each run, never persist one as a long-lived API key.
Rotating the client secret immediately invalidates client credentials tokens but does NOT revoke individual workspaces' access/refresh tokens, which keep working.

Granular scopes exist beyond read/write (issues:create, comments:create, timeSchedule:write) plus agent scopes app:assignable (assignment becomes delegation) and app:mentionable. The admin scope 'should never be asked for unless absolutely needed'.
Linear for Agents APIs are in Developer Preview ('functionality may change'), and agent sessions should acknowledge with a 'thought' activity within 10 seconds.
prerequisites: A Linear workspace to own the app (a dedicated management workspace is highly recommended)
Your scope set and actor choice

steps.detail: Create a dedicated workspace for managing the app (recommended: every admin of the owning workspace has access to the application). In Settings > API, create the OAuth2 Application and configure the redirect callback URLs. Optionally enable webhooks (for agents, select the Agent session events category) and toggle on client credentials tokens if needed. The app's name and icon are how your agent appears in customer workspaces.
steps.title: Create the OAuth2 Application

steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the app settings into your secret storage.
steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Secret

steps.detail: Redirect the user to linear.app/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope (comma-separated, required; read is always present), state (always supply it), optional actor (user or app), optional prompt=consent (forces the consent screen; useful for connecting multiple workspaces), and optional PKCE (plain or S256). Verify state on the callback.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST to api.linear.app/oauth/token with code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code (under PKCE, client_secret is optional and code_verifier is required). Access tokens are valid 24 hours.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: Call the GraphQL API at api.linear.app/graphql with Authorization: Bearer. For app installs, run the viewer query to learn the app's unique per-workspace ID and store it alongside the access token (Linear 'highly recommends' this).
steps.title: Call the GraphQL API; store the per-workspace app ID

steps.detail: Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token; persist the latest. Revoke via POST api.linear.app/oauth/revoke with the token field. Rotate secrets from app settings if exposed (know the side effects listed in Nuances).
steps.title: Refresh and revoke

tagline: Modern OAuth2 with a choice most providers don't offer: act as the user, or install as an 'app user' agent identity in the workspace. No review anywhere, but the client-credentials and actor rules have sharp edges.

time.active: ~15 min of in-product setup + ~1-2 hrs of standard flow code
time.total: Same day; nothing to wait for
